items.t: Vitamin K1, IV, 10 mg · Administer as a slow IV injection. · Do not dilute or mix with other injectables.
Vitamin K1, oral, 10 to 20 mg. · Check INR at least 12 hours after vitamin K1 has been administered. Repeated doses should be guided by further INR (or
Vitamin K1, oral, 0.5 to 1.0 mg (one tenth of the normal dose). · A repeat dose may be given 12 to 24 hrs later if the INR remains ≥8.
Vitamin K, IM, 1 mg immediately after birth routinely. · Administer in the antero lateral aspect of the mid-thigh. PHC Ch6_Last updated 30 July 2026
Vitamin K1, IV/oral, 1–5 mg/dose administered slowly.
Vitamin K1, IV/oral, 1–5 mg/dose administered slowly 6 hourly.
Vitamin K1, IM, 1 mg as a single dose.
Vitamin K1, IM, single dose at birth. Full term newborns: 1 mg. Preterm newborns: 0.5 mg.
Vitamin K1 (phytomenadione), oral, 2–5 mg three times weekly. · Monitor INR and titrate dose accordingly. · In the presence of cholestatic jaundice vitamin K should be given
Vitamin K1 (phytomenodione), IV, 2.5–10 mg daily. · Monitor response to vitamin K1 with INR and PTT.

cautions.t: Onset takes hours – give plasma as well for major bleeding

adverse_effects.t: Anaphylactoid reaction with rapid IV injection
